references.name: Abraham Lincoln
Charles Schwab
references.connection:
First million-dollar salary in America;
  Andrew Carnegie chose him for people skills,
  not steel knowledge; “hearty in
  approbation, lavish in praise”; the
  chalk-on-the-floor challenge story

references.name: Theodore Roosevelt
references.connection:
Studied every guest’s interests the
  night before; greeted servants by name;
  split Republican party over criticism of
  Taft; embodied genuine interest in
  people

references.name: Benjamin Franklin
references.connection:
Blunt and offensive in youth; a Quaker
  friend’s rebuke transformed him;
  forbade all “dogmatical
  expressions” and replaced certainty
  with tentativeness; became America’s
  greatest diplomat

references.name: Andrew Carnegie
references.connection:
Knew little about steel; named companies
  after others to win their loyalty; epitaph:
  “Here lies one who knew how to get
  around him men who were cleverer than
  himself”

references.name: William James
references.connection:
“The deepest principle in human
  nature is the craving to be
  appreciated”; “we are making
  use of only a small part of our physical
  and mental resources”

references.name: John Dewey
references.connection:
Identified “the desire to be
  important” as the deepest urge in
  human nature

references.name: Sigmund Freud
references.connection:
Everything springs from two motives: the
  sex urge and the desire to be great

references.name: B.F. Skinner
references.connection:
Animals rewarded for good behavior learn
  faster than animals punished for bad
  behavior — same applies to humans;
  minimize criticism, emphasize
  praise

references.name: Socrates
references.connection:
“Gadfly of Athens” who changed
  human thought by asking questions opponents
  had to agree with, never telling them they
  were wrong

references.name: Lao-tse
references.connection:
“Rivers and seas receive the homage
  of mountain streams because they keep below
  them”; “He who treads softly
  goes far”

references.name: Carl Rogers
references.connection:
Our first reaction to statements is
  evaluation/judgement rather than
  understanding; permitting yourself to
  understand is enormously valuable

references.name: James Harvey Robinson
references.connection:
Most “reasoning” is finding
  arguments for going on believing as we
  already do

references.name: Harry A. Overstreet
references.connection:
“Action springs out of what we
  fundamentally desire”; the
  “No” response creates physical
  withdrawal in the whole organism

references.name: Frederic Herzberg
references.connection:
Found the most motivating factor is the
  work itself, not money or
  conditions

references.name: Lowell Thomas
references.connection:
Wrote the biographical essay; traveled with
  Lawrence in Arabia; Carnegie’s close
  friend who encouraged him at bridge and
  beyond

references.name: Colonel Edward M. House
references.connection:
Planted ideas casually and let Wilson claim
  them; wanted results, not credit

references.name: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
references.connection:
“Hurting a man in his dignity is a
  crime”
